Attributed GitHub evidence; this record does not establish the owner’s experience.
Repository: anit0607/ai-journey-studio
Commit: 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1
Note: docs/build-notes/studio-progress.md

## Verified progress
- Documented assistant-observed database configuration, scheduler behavior and provider status on 25 October 2026; these are system observations, not the owner's personal experiences or feelings.
- Verified that the existing Neon Free account had a monthly allowance of 100 compute-unit hours per project.
- Verified that the production endpoint was configured with both minimum and maximum compute at 0.25 compute units and a five-minute autosuspend delay.
- Documented two sources of database reads in the previous setup: two-minute integration requests and five-second signed-in dashboard polling.
- Updated signed integration-request handling to validate the request and return before database access when outside the configured source-intake and publishing windows.
- Updated source intake to use hourly windows and publication handling to use exact configured windows.
- Updated background dashboard polling to pause when the page is hidden or unfocused, or after 60 seconds without activity; polling remains available when the page is active and recently used.
- Verified that fresh Neon provider observations reported at 04:10:55 UTC and 04:12:20 UTC on 25 October 2026 showed the production endpoint as SUSPENDED; these are reported observation times, not suspension event timestamps.
- Verified that a fresh Neon observation reported at 04:14:50 UTC again showed SUSPENDED; a separate Upstash metadata observation recorded the scheduled 04:12 integration wake as SUCCESS, without establishing a response body, HTTP status code or request-level SQL trace.
- Documented that the observation used provider status reads without SQL queries, manual resume or settings changes during the observation window.
- Documented that the verification used the existing connected account and Free plan, without a paid-plan upgrade.
- Documented the limits of this result: the checks establish endpoint state at the observed times, not uninterrupted sleep, measured monthly compute savings, guaranteed use within the Free allowance or successful LinkedIn publication.
- Documented that the commit linked below identifies the implementation change; the endpoint settings and runtime observations above come from separately inspected provider receipts, not from treating a commit link as runtime proof.

## Evidence

SOURCE DATE: 2026-10-25 REPOSITORY: anit0607/ai-journey-studio COMMIT: 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1 URL: https://github.com/anit0607/ai-journey-studio/commit/e2a608b9f7a9e1dfde4f96709e8cb47a182819ff

Documented on 25 October 2026 in the anit0607/ai-journey-studio repository, the project faced managing database workload within strict limits of the Neon Free plan, which allows 100 compute-unit hours per month per project. To control resource use, the production endpoint was set with fixed minimum and maximum compute of 0.25 compute units and a five-minute autosuspend delay.

The system previously triggered database reads from two sources: integration requests every two minutes and signed-in dashboard polling every five seconds. To reduce unnecessary load, the handling of signed integration requests was updated to validate the request time and return early without accessing the database if they fell outside configured intake and publishing windows. Source intake was aligned to hourly windows, while publication handling used exact configured windows. Dashboard polling was modified to pause when the page was hidden, unfocused, or after 60 seconds without activity, resuming only when the page was active and recently used.

Observations on the Neon provider status confirmed that the production endpoint was in a SUSPENDED state at multiple checked times (04:10:55, 04:12:20, and 04:14:50 UTC), indicating the autosuspend was active without manual intervention or SQL queries triggering wake events during that period. Meanwhile, a separate Upstash metadata check showed the scheduled 04:12 integration wake occurred successfully but without any SQL query trace or response data.

The documented limit of this approach is that the observations confirm the endpoint state at sampled times, but do not guarantee uninterrupted suspension duration or direct measurement of monthly compute savings within the free plan allowance. Also, these checks do not confirm successful external publication events such as LinkedIn posts.

This episode demonstrates a systematic method of tuning endpoint compute allocation and query scheduling, coupled with conditional early request return and adaptive polling, to comply with free-tier provider limits. The result is a suspended endpoint state during inactivity, observed remotely without interference, but with recognized limits on interpretability and guaranteed continuous savings.

(Source: anit0607/ai-journey-studio, commit 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1, documented 25 October 2026)

On 25 October 2026, the anit0607/ai-journey-studio project documented database and scheduler settings used to manage load within the Neon Free plan limits, which allow 100 compute-unit hours monthly per project. The production database endpoint was configured with fixed minimum and maximum compute units set to 0.25, along with an autosuspend delay of five minutes.

Previously, database reads occurred from two main sources: integration requests every two minutes and dashboard polling every five seconds when signed in. To reduce resource use during inactivity, the integration request handling was updated to check request timing against configured intake and publishing windows and return early without accessing the database if the request fell outside those windows. Intake was managed using hourly windows, while publishing used exact configured windows.

Dashboard polling in the background was changed to pause when the page was hidden, unfocused, or idle for more than 60 seconds. It resumed only if the page was active and had recent user interaction.

Status observations from the Neon provider at three separate times confirmed the production endpoint was in a SUSPENDED state without manual resume or executing SQL during those intervals. Separately, the Upstash metadata showed a scheduled 04:12 integration wake succeeded but did not involve SQL queries or return response data.

These observations were made using the existing Neon Free account without upgrading plans. The documentation notes that while these checks confirm the endpoint’s suspension state at specific times, they do not guarantee continuous suspension, exact monthly compute savings, or successful external publications such as LinkedIn posts.

This episode illustrates a practical approach to controlling database compute and request scheduling by aligning request windows and adapting polling behavior to reduce unnecessary load, resulting in observable endpoint suspension during inactivity under free-tier constraints.

(Source: anit0607/ai-journey-studio, commit 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1, documented 25 October 2026)

### LinkedIn

On 25 October 2026, the anit0607/ai-journey-studio project documented how it managed a production database endpoint within the strict limits of the Neon Free plan, which offers 100 compute-unit hours per month per project. To control resource use, the production endpoint was configured with both minimum and maximum compute fixed at 0.25 compute units and an autosuspend delay of five minutes.

Previously, database reads originated from two main sources: integration requests occurring every two minutes, and signed-in dashboard polling every five seconds. To reduce unnecessary database load, the system updated its handling of signed integration requests to first validate the request timing against configured intake and publishing windows. If the request fell outside these windows, it returned early without accessing the database. Intake was managed on hourly windows, while publishing followed exact configured time windows.

Additionally, dashboard polling was modified to pause when the page was hidden or unfocused, or when no user activity occurred for more than 60 seconds. Polling resumed only when the page became active and recently used.

Provider status checks at three distinct times confirmed the production endpoint was in a SUSPENDED state without manual intervention or SQL queries that could have triggered a wake event. Separately, an Upstash metadata observation verified that the scheduled integration wake at 04:12 UTC succeeded but involved no SQL query trace or response body.

This verification used an existing Neon Free account without any paid upgrade. The documentation notes that these observations only confirm the endpoint's suspension state at sampled times—they do not prove uninterrupted suspension, exact compute savings, or successful LinkedIn postings.

This episode reflects a practical configuration strategy for balancing database compute allocation and request scheduling to comply with free-tier limits. It aligns request processing to specific time windows and adapts polling behavior to pause during inactivity, resulting in observable endpoint suspension without manual or SQL trigger intervention.

(Source: anit0607/ai-journey-studio, commit 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1, documented 25 October 2026)
